searchText: Is there more information available why Ethash validation broke? I tried to find an issue on Neterhmind's github for that, but failed. Also the release notes are a bit sparse. I am confused why one would need a "heuristic" for hash function. Or is it the difficulty of the PoW aspect of it? There will be an announcement for it soonish I think. They want to wait until most people updated their nodes Where/What's the latest work on setting the gas limit per block post-merge? I was hoping to advocate for a monotonically increasing gas limit over time if node operators won't be voting on it anymore but I haven't read current proposals yet. indefinitely increasing gas limit is unwise it very likely will increase just because the game theory is different now but it would be a very bad idea to increase it massively What's your rationale? <dannyryan> Gas limit mechanism will remain untouched at the merge. Meaning pos block proposers rather than pow miners have the lever in their block construction Hardware/Network capacity should increase over time. And I think we all agree that the gas limit should increase over time in some fashion. Currently it's increased in big increments at network upgrades. But we could schedule in a conservative increase over time that more predictable. For the sake of discussion, say 5-15% increase per year. That also makes it easier for node operators to schedule hardware replacement as well. increases over time aren't predictable and Moore's law is essentially at its end real increases in performance right now are mainly from improving client implementation, which also isn't something we can rely on mathematically Are you saying that it's not realistic to expect clients to be able to handle 5% gas inflation a year? a sustainable network long term should not rely on the expectation that users buy new hardware on a regular basis with a floating gas limit this can be adjusted on an as-needed basis this should really be in <#595721451651465227> Sorry that's why I was curious if there was a discussion on-going somewhere else already.

excerpts.content:
Where/What's the latest work on setting the gas limit per block post-merge?
I was hoping to advocate for a monotonically increasing gas limit over time if node operators won't be voting on it anymore but I haven't read current proposals yet.

excerpts.author: mightypenguin
excerpts.content:
Hardware/Network capacity should increase over time. And I think we all agree that the gas limit should increase over time in some fashion.
Currently it's increased in big increments at network upgrades.
But we could schedule in a conservative increase over time that more predictable.
For the sake of discussion, say 5-15% increase per year.
That also makes it easier for node operators to schedule hardware replacement as well.

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: increases over time aren't predictable and Moore's law is essentially at its end

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: real increases in performance right now are mainly from improving client implementation, which also isn't something we can rely on mathematically

excerpts.author: mightypenguin
excerpts.content: Are you saying that it's not realistic to expect clients to be able to handle 5% gas inflation a year?
